questions.q: Northfield's Operations Manager asks "which product category sold the most?" about a month of CSV files already sitting in S3. What's the first real step?
options: Tell the Operations Manager the files need to be reformatted first
Clarify what "sold the most" means — units, revenue, or both — before writing any query
Immediately build a Glue ETL job to clean the files
Load the files into Redshift so the question can be answered with SQL
questions.explain: A category can sell huge unit volumes of cheap items while a pricier category earns more revenue, so the vague ask has to be clarified into a specific, answerable metric first.

questions.q: Why does this Beginner project deliberately stop at S3 + Glue Crawler + Athena instead of also building a Glue ETL job and loading Redshift?
options: Glue ETL jobs and Redshift aren't available in all AWS regions
There's one ad-hoc question, not a recurring reporting workload, so the extra pipeline stages would solve a problem Northfield doesn't have yet
CSV files can only ever be queried directly from S3, never transformed
Athena cannot query data that has passed through a Glue ETL job
questions.explain: Matching the build to the actual ask matters — a one-time question against 31 files doesn't need a transformation job or a data warehouse.

questions.q: What does "schema-on-read" mean in the context of this project's stack?
options: Every file must be converted to a strict schema before it can be uploaded to S3
The Glue Crawler deletes any file that doesn't match a predefined schema
Structure (columns, types) is applied when the data is queried, not when it's stored
Athena rewrites the raw CSV files into a new schema automatically
questions.explain: The raw CSV files stay exactly as they are in S3; the Glue Data Catalog and Athena apply structure only at query time.

questions.q: What is the Glue Data Catalog's role in this pipeline?
options: It is a separate database that physically stores a copy of every row from the CSV files
It automatically emails a report to the stakeholder once a query finishes
It replaces S3 as the storage location for the raw files
It stores table metadata (names, columns, types) that points at the files in S3, without moving or copying the data
questions.explain: The Catalog is metadata only — the actual data never leaves the S3 raw zone.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly OUT of scope for this Beginner project, per the lesson?
options: Querying the cataloged table directly with Athena
Running a Glue Crawler against the raw S3 files
Answering one specific stakeholder question about August's order data
A Glue ETL transformation job and a Redshift load
questions.explain: ETL and Redshift are saved for later projects, once there's a recurring, repeatable reporting need rather than a single ad-hoc question.
